page: Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-1 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance featuring 1 vCPU and 4.0 GB of system memory, which equates to 3.75 GB of memory per core. Powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.3 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, this instance provides a single dedicated physical core and a single thread. The CPU cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.25 MB of L2 cache, and 45 MB of L3 cache. It supports hardware features such as AVX, AES cryptography, BMI2, and FMA, but lacks AVX-512 extensions. This instance does not include bundled local storage or GPU accelerators, and comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results place the n1-standard-1 in the lower tiers of performance. Single-core and multi-core CPU performance tests via stress-ng yield a score of 1088.79, categorizing the processing power as weak. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with read-only small block cached speeds at 80.25 GB/sec and uncached large block read and write speeds dropping to 10.68 GB/sec and 9.71 GB/sec respectively. Geekbench testing reflects these constraints, showing a single-core score of 895.0 and a multi-core score of 898.0, with low performance across software compilation, ray tracing, and image processing workloads.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the n1-standard-1 offers a low-entry hardware profile suitable for lightweight, non-critical tasks where resource density and high throughput are not required. Its static web serving throughput is measured at 1.21 GB/sec, and small-scale LLM inference using a 135M model achieves 96.03 tokens/sec for prompt processing and 41.77 tokens/sec for text generation. Given these performance trade-offs, the instance is best suited for basic general-purpose workloads, lightweight background utilities, development testing, or simple web serving rather than intensive database operations or data science tasks.
